labeling_metadata.notes: Labelled by Uttam with the help of Claude and screenshots of the live pages, 2026-10-10. Claude read the pages and drafted evidence and values; Uttam took the screenshots, checked the quotes against the live pages and made the final decisions. Pipeline not run, data/ not opened. Home page read rendered in Claude's browser pane (innerText, alt and aria-label attributes); pricing, about, enterprise, safety, privacy-policy, eu-us-data-privacy-framework-policy, terms-of-use, customer-stories and agents/integrations were read as server-sent page text via fetch from the open page, not as rendered views. Geography: the home-page 'Trusted by leading developers and enterprises' strip visible from Uttam's location (India) lists Meesho, Cars24, Pocket FM, Mahindra & Mahindra, Razorpay, TVS Motor, EXL Service, Physics Wallah, Urban Company, Eternal by Zomato, Havells, JioStar, 99acres, Great Learning, Twilio, The Walt Disney Studios, KPN; a second, hidden set (Stripe, Telus, Cisco, Epic Games, NVIDIA, Revolut, Meta, Zoom, Square, Ramp, IBM, Deutsche Telekom, Klarna, Harvey, Salesforce) is in the HTML and on /customer-stories; the label uses the visible set, capped at 15 by page order; 'IDFC-logo.svg' is a filename, not a name, so excluded. Customer names are accessible-name link text on logo tiles (visually hidden), accepted like the title/aria-label precedent. Headquarters: the about page says 'as it expands London HQ' inside a news headline; the privacy policy and terms give 169 Madison Ave #2484, New York as a Data Protection Office / legal-notice address only (Decision (d) address, not used). This is a judgment call. Pricing: the pricing page default is the Creative tab (Free to Business plus Enterprise); Agents and API tabs have other views not captured; first-month promos ($1 Starter until Oct 18, $11 Creator) and annual billing (10x monthly) are not plans; Startup Grants Program is not a plan. free_trial: the Free plan is a free tier and 'Try v4 with 2x credits for two weeks' is a paid-plan promotion, not a trial. Certifications: FedRAMP 20x Class A is from a dated About-page headline (1 Oct 2026); EU-US Data Privacy Framework (borderline programme) from its dedicated policy page, eu-us-data-privacy-framework-policy (the privacy policy spells it 'EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework'); HIPAA-eligible configurations are law/eligibility, not a certification, so excluded under Decision (a); the Trust Center (compliance.elevenlabs.io) is a separate domain and was not followed. Partnerships: named in visible text as partner/partnership/strategic agreement; excluded: Deutsche Telekom, IBM, Salesforce (partnership only in URL slug or no partnership wording in text), Ukrainian public services (not a single named partner), investors and integrations (Zapier, Stripe, Twilio, etc.) under Decision (b). Products: the three platforms, the Products-menu items and 'Dubbing'; excluded: model versions (Eleven v3, v4, Flash, Multilingual, Turbo, Scribe, Eleven Music, Music v2, Dubbing v2), Dubbing Studio, Productions, Flows, Voice Library, Iconic Marketplace, Integrations, API Reference, API Key and vertical pages. Industries: 'Customer Support' (agents menu) is a use case, so excluded. named_alternatives: no comparison or alternatives pages in the menus or footer; blog not searched.

labeling_instructions.source_policy: Use only information the company states on its own public website. No outside knowledge, no assumptions.

statuses.extracted: Directly stated on the site, with a verbatim (or near-verbatim) quote as evidence.
statuses.inferred: Allowed ONLY on the three whitelisted fields below. A reasonable read of stated evidence, not a direct quote.
statuses.not_found: The site does not provide sufficient evidence for this field.
statuses.conflicting: Two pages give genuinely incompatible values for the SAME single-valued attribute (see conflicting_vs_union rule below).

labeling_instructions.multi_value_evidence_rule: For any field in this list -- products.names, customers.industries, traction.named_customers, traction.certifications, traction.partnerships, comparisons.named_alternatives, pricing.public_plans -- check every value item against the evidence text individually. If one contiguous quote does not literally contain every item, make 'evidence' a list of quotes in the same order as 'value' (evidence[i] must support value[i]) instead of writing one summary sentence. Never let a paraphrase stand in as evidence for a list.
labeling_instructions.conflicting_vs_union_rule: Use 'conflicting' only for a single-valued field (e.g. company_identity.headquarters) where two pages state incompatible facts. For a list-valued field, do NOT mark it conflicting just because two pages list different or overlapping items -- merge every genuinely-sourced item into one list instead.

field_specific_rules.customers.segments: Single string. How the company classifies buyers by structure/size (individual, team, SMB, mid-market, enterprise, nonprofit, government). Stays a single string -- do not turn into a list.
field_specific_rules.customers.industries: List. The named verticals, sectors, or professions the site explicitly says it serves. Each item must be a term the site itself uses, not a category you infer.
field_specific_rules.products.names: List. Counts only if the company treats the text as a proper name for something it sells: a nav item linking to its own product page, a product-page title/heading, or explicit 'Introducing X' branding. A descriptive phrase ('our platform') does not count. Tiebreaker: does the term have its own page/URL on the site?
field_specific_rules.pricing.sales_motion: Inference allowed. 'Contact sales' with no public amounts -> sales-led (inferred). Do not infer subscription pricing from 'Contact sales' alone.
field_specific_rules.pricing.revenue_model: Inference allowed, but only from a structural signal the site states outright (per seat, monthly subscription, transaction fee, one-time license). Never infer from company type/category alone.
field_specific_rules.products.delivery_model: Inference allowed, but only from the site's own words describing how the product is delivered (self-serve, managed service, app download, physical + install). Never infer from category assumptions.
field_specific_rules.pricing.free_trial: Single string. Quote the site's own trial/demo phrasing verbatim (e.g. '14-day free trial, no credit card required'). Never normalize to yes/no.
field_specific_rules.traction.certifications: List. Compliance/standards marks (SOC 2, ISO, ...) or named partner-tier badges issued by a third party.
field_specific_rules.traction.partnerships: List. Named companies described as integration, channel, or technology partners.
field_specific_rules.traction.named_customers: List. Entities described as using/buying the product (logos, 'trusted by', case studies, testimonials). A name may legitimately appear in both this field and partnerships/certifications if the site describes it both ways -- that's not an error.
